# sv0vm multi-implementation expansion (VMX)

## purpose

Turn `.sv0b` from "whatever `sv0c` emits and the SML VM accepts" into a
normative, versioned, machine-checked contract, then deliver **six
independent conforming VMs** (sv0, Go, Haskell, Python, C99, TypeScript/Node)
that share one conformance system. The SML/NJ VM becomes a restricted
positive-only oracle and is archived after VMX R0.6.

The governing document is:

- `~/Documents/project-specs/sv0vm-implementation-expand/SPEC.md`: version
  `0.1.36` (draft governing spec; 0.1.36 adds DEC-030..032, 2026-09-27), audit baseline 2026-09-02 (meta
  `f67a1a8`, sv0c `803c3c0`, sv0vm `50d355d`, sv0doc `a6643f5`), with
  candidate refreshes through DEC-028 and a 2026-09-25 cross-note reserving
  opcode 119 for sv0cov `COVER_HIT`. 32 decisions, all accepted (DEC-012 merged
  into DEC-002).

This file is the planning **hub**. The slice index is
**`task/sv0vm-multi-implementation-checklist.Rmd`** (`VMX-###`). Closure
authority is SPEC §26 (gates F0, R0.x, R0.5, R0.6, SML retirement, R1), §24
(requirement catalog), and Appendix D (per-implementation definition of done).

VMX is tracked in `task/milestone-orientation.json` as `VMX` because its F0
changes the **producer** (`sv0c`) and the **normative bytecode docs**
(`sv0doc`), not only the `sv0vm` repo. It also supplies the standalone VM that
the installed-toolchain release needs (`task/sv0-toolchain-interface-distribution.Rmd` D-3).

## ownership (SPEC §3.3, DEC-001)

| Concern | Owner |

| Container layout, opcode numbers, operands, stack effects, traps, built-in IDs | `sv0doc/bytecode/` (after the F0 extraction) |
| Bytecode emission and producer compatibility | `sv0c/lib/bytecode.sv0`, `sv0c/lib/vm_codegen.sv0` |
| Registries (`spec/opcodes.json`, `builtins.json`, `errors.json`), schemas, conformance corpus, runners | `sv0vm/spec/`, `sv0vm/conformance/` |
| Six implementations | `sv0vm/implementations/{sv0,go,haskell,python,c99,typescript}/` (same repo, DEC-001) |
| SML reference (source + history kept through R1; out of active CI after R0.6) | `sv0vm` (existing `src/` or `reference/sml/`; the maintainer chooses) |
| Workspace parity commands and CI wiring | `sv0-toolchain` |

## observed drift since the SPEC audit (re-checked 2026-09-27; sv0vm `1c9c3d4`, sv0c `19c3c24`)

The spec's validated baseline is 2026-09-02. The toolchain has moved since.
Each row must be reconciled at F0 (SPEC §3.1 requires a clean attributable
rerun before a new baseline is adopted).

| # | Spec position | Observed now | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| G-1 | Unsigned ops get registry allocations only after the full u64 inventory freezes (U64-006, DEC-005). Before R0.5, the producer **rejects** source `u64` for the VM target (U64-003). | Producer + SML already implement unsigned-wide opcodes 38–39 (div/mod), 40–42 (wide shifts), 43–45 (wide AND/OR/XOR), 70–73 (unsigned compares), and the producer emits them for `u64`. | These are candidate allocations. F0 must either adopt them into the frozen `sv0vm-v1-u64` inventory or renumber them. Until R0.5, VM-target `u64` emission contradicts U64-003, so the gate needs a decision: adopt early, or add a temporary producer rejection. See D-2. |
| G-2 | Core built-ins 0–14, hostfs 15–17; slice built-ins proposed at 30–34 (§3.1 refresh). | SML dispatches built-ins through **42**: slices 30–34, string↔byte 35/36, `fill_explicit` 37, f64 vec 38–40, index sugar 41/42 (all shipped for sv0-strings/mathlib). | `builtins.json` must classify 18–42 into profiles the spec does not yet define. **Spec amendment needed** before registry freeze. See D-1. |
| G-3 | DEC-015: `string_char_at` traps (`ETRAP_BOUNDS`) for any `i ≥ len`, identically in both backends and all VMs. | C runtime `sv0_str_char_at` and the SML VM both return **0 at `i == len`** on purpose. The self-hosted compiler's own scanners rely on that one-past-the-end idiom. | F0 producer migration with a large regression surface: every compiler scanner (lexer, parser, resolver, …) must stop reading at `len`. Needs its own careful slice series plus the self-host loop and stage0 goldens. |
| G-4 | DEC-004: `INT64_MIN / -1` = `INT64_MIN`, remainder 0, guarded in **every VM and the native C backend**. | Not guarded (C UB, SML `Overflow`). | Small producer/runtime change plus sanitizer fixtures. |
| G-5 | DEC-011: exactly one zero-arity `main`; both producers append explicit zero-slot unit returns; no reachable fallthrough; final stack is empty or exactly one `I32`. | SML VM stops at code end, takes the top `I32`, and ignores deeper cells. The producer relies on fallthrough in places. | Producer change (explicit terminators) + golden refresh (tier-2 byte parity changes). |
| G-6 | DEC-003: strict canonicality (no residue, gaps, overlap, trailing bytes, bool ∉ {0,1}). | All 97 retained goldens satisfied it at audit. New goldens since (u64, slices, f64 vec) are unchecked. | Rerun the strict decoder over the current corpus. |
| G-7 | Opcode 119 = `COVER_HIT`, only in coverage profiles; unknown in `sv0vm-v1-core`. | sv0vm CV-102 registry guard (`test/coverage-identifiers.json`) reserves it. | Consistent. Fold that guard into the F0 `opcodes.json`. |
| G-8 | Loader/verifier: bounded decode, whole-module verifier, limits, structured errors. | SML loader is unchecked, has no verifier and no limits, and uses a marker protocol (`SV0VM_RUN_BEGIN`/`vm_exit:`). | Expected. SML is not modernized (DEC-008 D). Only its adapter is restricted (ARC-001). |
| G-9 | sv0 implementation needs `try_read_bytes(path, max_bytes, out: Vec<byte>) -> i32` and run-scoped `Vec` reclamation (DEC-002 B). R1 needs `Result<Vec<byte>, ReadBytesError>` (Option A). | The C runtime has a process-global `Vec` handle table with no per-vector release or run reset. The byte↔string bridges (35/36) exist. | New runtime + builtin work in sv0c (Appendix C experiment). Option A also needs aggregate `Result` returns through native C. |

## cross-spec conflicts (resolved 2026-09-27)

| # | Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| X-1 | Installed-toolchain `sv0vm` (exact exit status, `-- args`, tool-info, readiness) versus the VMX CLI (classified status, result file, no args). | Two surfaces. The installed `sv0vm` wraps one conforming library; `sv0vm-<lang>` stays the conformance CLI. VMX `0.1.36` DEC-030 + TID `0.1.1-draft` DEC-064 (VM-007). |
| X-2 | VMX hostfs is deny-by-default; `sv0 run --backend=vm` has no grant surface. | BR1 `sv0vm` claims `sv0vm-v1-core` only and rejects hostfs built-ins at verification. File I/O is native-only in BR1 (TID DEC-065, VM-008). |
| X-3 | VMX retires SML after R0.6; TID BR1 needs a native VM. | The TID R0 preview bundles the SML runtime. BR1 ships the C99 library (`VMX-402` → `TID-305`). |

## decisions (resolved 2026-09-27; SPEC DEC-001..032 all accepted)

| ID | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D-1 | How do built-ins 18–42 enter the frozen registry? | **Named profiles** (VMX DEC-031, §2.3): `sv0vm-v1-slices` (30–34), `sv0vm-v1-bytes` (35–37, requires slices), `sv0vm-v1-f64vec` (38–42). IDs 18–29 are unallocated, and an unknown built-in fails verification. Semantics are extracted into sv0doc at F0 (`VMX-003`). |
| D-2 | Keep or renumber the shipped u64 opcodes? | **Freeze the inventory now and adopt 38–45/70–73 where they fit** (VMX DEC-032). Until R0.5, the producer emits them only under its `sv0vm-v1-u64` profile flag (output marked non-core) and otherwise rejects source `u64` for the VM target (`VMX-102`). |
| D-3 | Move SML to `reference/sml/`? | **No.** Keep the current paths and label the tree reference-only in its README. |
| D-4 | Toolchain pins + CI budget | Pin exact Go / GHC+cabal / CPython minor / Node LTS / GCC+Clang. Full matrices run on pushes to `main`; PRs run a path-filtered subset. |

## sequencing

- **Do now (parallel with M5): VMX F0 spec/registry/corpus (`VMX-0xx`).** It
  gives the toolchain its first complete normative bytecode spec (sv0doc
  `bytecode/format.md` and `instructions.md` are indexes today). It does not
  change compiler output.
- **Producer migrations (`VMX-1xx`) are toolchain-affecting.** Schedule them
  like compiler work, one slice at a time, with the self-host loop plus tier-2
  goldens. DEC-015 (G-3) is the largest and riskiest; keep it last in the band.
- **The six ports (`VMX-2xx`..`5xx`) are independent of M5** and mostly live in
  the sv0vm repo. The C99 port (`VMX-4xx`) is on the installed-toolchain BR1
  critical path (TID D-3: the BR1 `sv0vm` wraps the C99 library, `TID-305`).
- **R0.5/R0.6** touch the producer again (u64 profile gating, v2 signatures
  from checked IR). Sequence them after M5 so the LLVM backend's type mapping
  and the v2 VM-cell signatures do not diverge.
